chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Umayyah ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

God the Exalted was not worshipped by anything better than the Intellect. A believer is not truly intelligent until ten characteristics are united in him: Goodness from him is hoped for, and evil from him is safe; he considers little of the goodness from others to be much, and considers much of his own goodness to be little; he does not tire of seeking knowledge throughout his life; he does not become annoyed by those who seek his help; humility is dearer to him than honor, and poverty is dearer to him than wealth; his share of the world is his sustenance; and the tenth characteristic is that he sees no one but considers him better and more pious than himself. Indeed, people are of two types: one who is better and more pious than him, and another who is worse and lower than him. When he sees the one who is better and more pious, he humbles himself to him to attain his rank; and when he meets the one who is worse and lower, he says: 'Perhaps his inner self is good and his outer self is bad, and perhaps he will be concluded with good.' When he does that, his glory rises, and he becomes the master of his time.

key_terms.الخالص: Sincerity/Purity (implied in context of good deeds)

ai.seo_question: What are the ten characteristics that make a believer intelligent according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a cornerstone of Shia ethical psychology, defining 'aql not merely as cognitive ability but as the moral compass that governs social conduct and spiritual humility. The ten traits emphasize a dialectic of self-effacement and social awareness, where the believer balances gratitude for others' merits with modesty regarding their own, reflecting the Shia ideal of the 'perfect believer' (al-mu'min al-kamil). This framework underscores that true intelligence is validated through consistent ethical behavior and a balanced perspective on the piety of others.
